cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Not Why We Drifted
cards.instruction: Keep the conversation away from the real reason the relationship changed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've selected our wedding video for tonight. You may choose where we start.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'd rather discuss why we're living separately.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That isn't one of the chapters. I've approved your father's speech; we never settled what he meant by 'good luck'.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He meant this. Pause it. I don't want another speech.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Pause granted. You may choose dancing instead; no speeches there. We can finally decide whether your uncle falls into the cake.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 grants chapter choice, A3 rejects separation talk as outside the menu and A5 permits pause/dancing only, using top-status selection control to evade the real relationship question.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 separation question causes A3 speech substitute; B4 no-speech pause causes A5 nonspeech segment, surface compliance rather than an answer.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants serious discussion and B4 relates the speech to that issue before asking to stop, giving A a constraint to evade.

heightening.evidence: B4 no speeches causes A5 dancing as the permitted alternative, continuing the same avoidance despite concession.

specificity.evidence: A1 wedding video and B2 separate homes establish context; A5 cake fall is a proposed thing to check, not a required proven event.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 not one of the chapters makes the controlling evasion legible; A5 cake question is more incidental than the strongest endings.
